title: VC Valuation: Pre-Money to Exit
description: Master advanced VC valuation mechanics including pre/post-money calculations, option pool shuffles, and multi-round dilution analysis.

interactions.prompt: Series B term sheet: $20M investment, $80M pre-money, 20% unallocated option pool to be created pre-close. Founders currently own 60% of 10M shares. What's the real effective pre-money valuation for existing shareholders?

options.text: $80M — the stated pre-money is the effective valuation
$64M — option pool reduces effective pre-money by $16M
$60M — founders' share defines the effective valuation
$100M — you should use post-money as the reference

interactions.prompt: You're a Series A lead. A SaaS startup has $3M ARR growing 3x YoY but 18-month runway at current burn. They want $50M pre-money. A competitor offers $40M pre-money with full ratchet anti-dilution. Which term do you counter with?

options.text: $45M pre-money with broad-based weighted average anti-dilution
$50M pre-money with 2x participating preferred and pay-to-play
$40M pre-money with no anti-dilution but 1x non-participating preferred
$50M pre-money with full ratchet matching the competitor's offer

interactions.prompt: In the VC method, if a startup's expected exit value is $500M in 5 years and the VC targets 10x gross return, the implied ____ valuation today is $50M, but after a 15% option pool expansion pre-money the effective founder valuation drops to $____.

options.text: post-money; $42.5M
pre-money; $42.5M
post-money; $35M
pre-money; $35M

interactions.prompt: Fintech startup metrics: $8M ARR, 140% net revenue retention, 70% gross margin, -$5M FCF, $2B TAM. Comparable public companies trade at 15x NTM revenue. Recent private round comps show 20-25x for similar growth. Which data point most warrants a premium or discount to comps?

options.text: 70% gross margin is standard — neutral impact on multiple
140% NRR signals exceptional expansion — justifies premium to comps
$2B TAM limits upside — warrants a discount to comps
Negative FCF indicates unsustainable model — apply steep discount

interactions.prompt: Rank these factors from MOST to LEAST important when determining a Series C valuation for a $30M ARR enterprise SaaS company preparing for IPO in 18 months.

options.text: Comparable public company NTM revenue multiples
Expected IPO discount and time-to-liquidity adjustment
Historical private round step-up ratios
Rule of 40 score (growth rate + FCF margin)

interactions.prompt: A D2C brand at $15M revenue (growing 80% YoY) needs $25M. Offer A: $100M pre-money from a top-tier fund with 1x participating preferred + 3x cap. Offer B: $75M pre-money from a strategic acquirer (major retailer) with standard 1x non-participating preferred. Which maximizes founder outcome at a $400M exit?

options.text: Offer A — higher valuation offsets participation at $400M exit
Offer B — non-participating converts; founders keep more above preference
Offer A — participating preferred capped at 3x limits investor take
Offer B — strategic partner accelerates exit likelihood enough to compensate

interactions.prompt: The public SaaS index drops 40% over 3 months. Your portfolio company's Series C is mid-process at $500M pre-money based on 25x NTM revenue. The lead investor now proposes a structured deal: $500M headline but with 1.5x liquidation preference and ratchet to IPO. How should you advise the founder?

options.text: Accept — headline valuation protects signaling for future rounds
Counter at $350M clean terms — avoid structure that punishes downside
Accept structure but negotiate ratchet to narrow-based weighted average
Pause fundraise entirely and extend runway with bridge debt

interactions.priorContext: Previously the company was raising at $500M pre-money in a strong market. Public SaaS multiples have now compressed 40%, making the original valuation unjustifiable on comps. The lead investor is offering structure to bridge the gap.

interactions.prompt: A pre-revenue biotech startup claims a $10B TAM. Rank these valuation approaches from MOST to LEAST appropriate for its Series A pricing.

options.text: Risk-adjusted DCF of pipeline with probability-weighted outcomes
Comparable precedent transaction multiples for similar-stage biotechs
VC method using peak revenue scenario and target return
TAM penetration model with revenue multiple on projected Year 5 sales
